thread:
mia.ae: Quick sync — FinReg wants a hybrid POC. On‑prem traffic -> our Private deployment in their VPC. They do TLS inspect and demand a small set of stable egress IPs to paste into their firewall. Also asking whether VPC peering or PrivateLink is the cleaner path. Any blockers?
ash.netops: We can support per-AZ static EIPs via an NLB + EIP setup. If traffic originates from our side NAT, we can publish EIPs. If we rely on the customer's NAT, they control egress.
ben.platform: TL;DR: PrivateLink is the lower-friction option for allowlisting (fewer route changes). Peering/transit gives broad L3 access but needs route table + security review. Also consider latency and bandwidth.
rachel.se: Customer questions we need to answer: 1) single-list of IPs to whitelist? 2) will TLS inspect break auth (token pinning)? 3) pricing impact for reserved EIPs / NAT throughput?
ben.platform: We can provide a curated EIP set (3‑5 addresses) in the region for the POC. Cost model: EIP allocation + per-GB egress if we egress traffic out of our infra. If they're in their VPC with Private deploy, likely zero extra from our side.
ash.netops: Notes on TLS inspect: if their proxy terminates TLS and re-encrypts with a corporate CA, that breaks our cert chain validation for client certs and token flows. Recommend TLS passthrough for our endpoints where possible. If passthrough impossible, customer must ensure their proxy preserves SNI and headers we use for auth.
mia.ae: They said BlueCorp proxy cannot be disabled. They asked if we accept adding their corporate CA to our trust store (so intercept won't break calls).
rachel.se: We do NOT add customer CAs to hosted environments. For Private deployments (VPC/on‑prem) the customer manages that trust. Workarounds: 1) Use our PrivateLink endpoint inside their VPC so traffic stays within their cloud and they can control TLS locally. 2) Provide IP-only allowlist and ask their proxy to whitelist our EIPs without MITM for those destinations.
sec-bot: Security checklist (internal): https://redwood.internal/security/poc-network-checklist : minimal rules for POC: allow outbound TCP 443 to our published EIPs. Example doc-range for tests: `203.0.113.0/24` and `198.51.100.0/24` (we'll give exact addresses).
ash.netops: Example firewall snippet they can drop into ASA / firewall: ```
permit tcp any host 203.0.113.12 eq 443
permit tcp any host 203.0.113.20 eq 443
permit tcp any host 198.51.100.5 eq 443
deny   ip  any any log
```
ben.platform: Quick curl test they can run from a proxy-host (use --resolve to avoid DNS): ```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood-poc.example:443:203.0.113.12 https://api.redwood-poc.example/health
```
mia.ae: Action items: 1) Ash to confirm EIP pool and provide exact addresses by EOD. 2) Ben to confirm any pricing delta for reserved EIPs/NAT. 3) Rachel to draft POC network diagram + send to customer.
ash.netops: I'll ping infra to reserve 3 EIPs in us-east-1 and return the list. Note: if they want per-AZ sticky egress, we'll allocate 3 (one/az).achel.se: I'll make the network diagram and include both flows: PrivateLink flow and Peering/Transit flow + notes on TLS inspect behavior.
mia.ae: Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll update FinReg with the temporary checklist and ask for a proxy-test host to run the curl check. 
sec-bot: Reminder — customer must sign the network contact form before we publish EIPs (audit trail). Link: https://redwood.internal/legal/network-contact-form
